correctness.rationale: Ordering the adjacent sides a>b gives a>c>b by the cosine law, and t=(a+c)/b>2 uniquely recovers the reduced m/n. The integer numerators are (m^2-n^2,n(2m-n),m^2-mn+n^2); parity excludes a common 2, and any odd common prime must divide both 2m-n and 3n^2, so can only be 3. When 3 divides m+n, C=(m+n)^2-3mn has 3-adic valuation 1. The perimeter is (m+n)(2m-n)/d, with the two factors sharing at most 3 and summing to 3m. For d=1 a square would make both factors coprime squares summing to 0 mod 3, impossible. For d=3 divide both factors by 3 to get coprime r,s, r<s<2r. Valuations of 3rs force the 3-times-square/square split with the other coordinate prime to 3; conversely this gives 3 not dividing r+s and gcd(r+s,2r-s)=1. The primitive side formulas and injectivity follow, and the equilateral primitive triangle has perimeter 3. Each uv<=Y wedge has area Y log(2)/4 by the ratio substitution; slicing on the unrestricted coordinate replaces length by (2/3)length+O(1) for the restricted coordinate and gives O(sqrt(Y)+1) total discrepancy. In the coprimality Möbius sum, 3-divisible divisors vanish, the remaining main terms have density (2/3) product_{p!=3}(1-p^-2)=3/(4 zeta(2)), and the errors for d up to O(sqrt(Y)) sum to O(sqrt(Y) log(2Y)), with tail O(sqrt(Y)). Both wedges and Y=sqrt(X)/3 then give 3 log(2)/(4 pi^2) and the stated error. My independent reduced-conic scan, r,s scan and direct perimeter-divisor reconstruction agree through 10^7 (branches/independent_small_replays.py triangle): counts 1,1,6,16,54,165 at the six recorded bounds, with distinct triples sharing perimeter 736164. These are finite checks, not the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The underlying unrestricted parameterization is known. In particular, the two square-factor families follow by elementary filtering of Zimhoni's exact classification, and should not be credited as a stand-alone new unrestricted classification or a hard consequence. The distinct supported contribution of the composite finding is the square-perimeter triangle count with its arithmetic leading constant and error term. The closest power-perimeter counting result treats a different angle and a different local density. Earlier potentially relevant printed texts remain incompletely checked.
residual_risks: No whole-paper exclusion for Gordon–Wells (2010), Gordon (2012), Gilder (1982), or Burn (2003); the full texts could contain an overlooked related specialization. An analogous right-angle result and a known 60-degree parameterization make the distinction specifically the evaluated sparse counting law, not the basic classification machinery.
